column1: # Hudhud's rights register (plan v1, Marhala 12; 25 Nov 2026): every source Hudhud's data, model or answers come from, used or planned.
# kind: own (the owner's or the app's own), ai-output (written by an AI in this project's sessions), outside (anyone else's).
# licence_checked: own; repo (the repository states it); well-established (widely documented, not re-read here); verify (a person
# must read the source's own terms before a release relies on it). status: used / planned / rejected.
# A row whose terms were read starts its notes with 'Verdict <date>: VERIFIED / RESTRICTED / STILL-VERIFY' and the URLs read.
# The script's licence_checked has no word for 'read' yet: a verified row whose subject is facts or a public formula says
# well-established; RESTRICTED and STILL-VERIFY rows keep 'verify', so --check still lists them as the backlog.
# scripts/hudhud_manifest.py --check fails when the data manifest names a source id that is not a row here, or a row is malformed.

column2: The Quran's Arabic text of the verses Hudhud shows (quran.com, quranworld.net, alim.org, tohed.com, read 14 Nov 2026)
column4: Not confirmed. The Quran's words are centuries old and owned by no one; a digitised edition's exact spelling and marks may carry its publisher's terms. The common standard, the Tanzil Quran text (CC BY 3.0, as its text files state), allows verbatim copies only, changing it is not allowed, with Tanzil.net named and linked. Read 26 Nov 2026: quran.com's terms could not be fetched in this session; alim.org's FAQ says nothing on reuse; no terms page was found for quranworld.net or tohed.com

The app does not change the text: the verses are stored as written and shown whole, joined only by line breaks; Hud 11:88 is shown as its last clause under the verse's number (an excerpt, not a change). HudhudStory also shows 27:26 and 27:44 from the same sources. To close: the owner names which edition the letters were copied from (quran.com usually serves the King Fahd Complex's Uthmani text) and reads that edition's terms; if Tanzil, add 'Text: Tanzil.net' with the link to the About page. Religious questions go to a qualified scholar (plan 'Never' 8).
